Robot stays offline unless you ask for a helper (“ask a helper …”, “go get Jarvis”) or let Robot check hard questions with one. Only text leaves the phone: your voice is turned into text here, and a helper\'s answer is read by Robot\'s voices.
By itself, Robot sends your question and the last two turns of the conversation, with any screen text, photo or what it read (%1$s is on).

By itself, Robot sends only your question and the last two turns of plain conversation. Once a conversation has screen text, a photo, or what Robot read from your contacts, calendar or notes, the weather (where you are) or your phone\'s status, it sends only your question (more for helpers you trust with personal content); anything more goes only after you tap a card that lists it.
Questions about news, prices or anything current go to %1$s by itself only when it can search the web; otherwise Robot answers and offers.

Daily budget: once it\'s reached, Robot asks before checking with a helper by itself until tomorrow. A helper whose prices Robot doesn\'t know isn\'t counted. Show cost: “≈ 1¢” under each helper\'s reply, estimated from the published prices (or the price the company reports); “cost unknown” when Robot can\'t tell.

Who should Robot be able to ask? A company\'s model needs an API key from that company (paid separately from any app subscription). Without a key, a company with an app on this phone gets your question in its app: you press Send there, and Robot doesn\'t hear the answer. A model on your own computer needs no key and costs nothing, and is private when the computer is yours. For another company, you enter its OpenAI-compatible address (https).

Is this computer yours, and does it run the model itself (not passing questions on to a company)? If yes, Robot can include what it read for you (your calendar, notes, contacts) when it asks %1$s. Your screen and photos still need a tap every time. You can change this on its page.
That isn\'t an address Robot can use: a name or IP address, with http:// or https:// if you like, and a port.
Robot connects to a company only with https://.
That address can\'t be a server.
The computer running Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, LocalAI or Open WebUI: its IP address or name, such as %1$s, %2$s or %3$s. Without a port, Robot tries the usual ones.
Without https, anyone on the same Wi-Fi can read what Robot sends. Fine on your home network; on a shared one, use Tailscale or https.
Anyone on the same Wi-Fi can read what Robot sends to %1$s. Use https or Tailscale on a network you share.
Anyone on the same Wi-Fi can read what Robot sends to %1$s, including the personal content you trust it with. Use https or Tailscale on a network you share.

For DeepSeek, High means its maximum.
%1$s\'s voice is a Kokoro voice, so you hear who is talking. With the Kitten voice helpers use Kitten\'s other voice; with the phone\'s voice, a lower pitch.

Trusted with personal content: off (the default), when Robot checks with %1$s by itself in a conversation that holds something personal (what Robot read from your calendar, notes or contacts, where you are, your phone\'s status), only your question goes; “go get %1$s” asks before including the conversation; a spoken yes never sends personal content. On: all of that goes to %1$s without asking. Your screen and photos still need a tap every time, and so does a conversation that had them.
